**Deviations from the skill spec (read first)**

- **The skill's required tool is not available.** `mcp__financekit__correlation_matrix` is not bound in this Cloud session, and neither are the `mcp__tradingview_advanced__*` or `mcp__yahoo_finance__*` tools the cron prompt lists for provenance.

- **Fallback used:** Yahoo Finance Chart API (`query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/{SYM}?range=6mo&interval=1d`), one call per proxy, reached through a cookie + crumb handshake (`fc.yahoo.com` cookie seed → `/v1/test/getcrumb`).
- A cookie-less request to the same endpoint returned **HTTP 429** on this egress, exactly as the runtime contract documents;
- the handshake returned HTTP 200 on the first attempt for all 8 symbols. Pearson correlations were then computed locally on daily log returns.
- This violates the skill's "compute only via `correlation_matrix`, do not compute manually" hard rule —
- the rule was not satisfiable in this environment, so the run continued on the fallback and stopped there rather than chaining to another MCP.

- It is used **only** to validate the Yahoo series, never to fill gaps.

- Returns are the standard basis and are the primary table below;
- the levels matrix is in the appendix because it produces materially different headline pairs (SPY–TLT is +0.33 on returns but -0.69 on levels).
- **The 2026-10-28 bar is excluded from the matrix.** The session was still in progress at 10:05 ET (SPY volume 3.19M vs 28.53M for the completed prior session), so a partial bar is not a close.
- Its effect is quantified below instead: adding it moves no pair by more than **0.0017**.
- **The WoW delta is a one-week roll of the window.** Last week's matrix used the trailing 127 sessions ending 2026-10-23; this one uses the trailing 127 sessions ending 2026-10-27.
- Same length, shifted one week — not an overlapping comparison.
- Correlation is **regime context only** — not causation, not a forecast.
- The audit line the skill asks for was **not** written: the Cloud cron prompt instructs that audit writes are skipped here.

**TL;DR**

- The correlation structure is **essentially unchanged from last week** —
- not one of the 28 pairs moved more than 0.0197 absolute, so this is a genuine "no regime shift" reading rather than a noisy one.
- Equities remain a single crowded bloc (SPY–QQQ +0.91, QQQ–EEM +0.88), implied vol still tracks equities inversely as always (SPY–^VIX -0.78), and the dollar remains the pivot proxy of the whole matrix (SPY–UUP -0.37, GLD–UUP -0.57).
- The one relationship that still matters for hedging is **QQQ–TLT at +0.20 (raw 0.195)** —
- the only pair in the matrix below the 0.20 line and the sole reason long duration is still cheap insurance against growth equity, though it has drifted up from +0.19 and is close to crossing back into "correlated" territory.

- What actually moved last week was **price, not structure**: QQQ added ~3.6 points of window return and GLD rebounded ~3.6 points off its lows, while the correlation network sat still.
- The stocks-bonds hedge remains broken (SPY–TLT +0.33, IWM–TLT +0.49 —
- both positive), and gold is still the worst-performing proxy in the universe at **-11.76%** over six months even after the bounce.

- A hawkish surprise would most plausibly show up in **GLD–UUP (-0.57)** and **SPY–TLT (+0.33)** — the two pairs that have historically carried the largest regime moves in this matrix.
